title: USC and Quantum Elements Demonstrate Surface Code Scaling on IBM Heavy-Hex Processors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: USC and Quantum Elements demonstrated on 156-qubit IBM Heron QPUs that subthreshold surface-code error suppression works on IBM's non-square heavy-hex lattice using a fold-unfold SWAP embedding and dynamical decoupling, while warning that unmitigated idle noise can produce false scaling claims.

themes.theme: Surface code scaling on non-native lattices

insights.claim: Researchers from USC and Quantum Elements demonstrated subthreshold surface code scaling on IBM's heavy-hex (honeycomb) lattice architecture using 156-qubit Heron-generation superconducting QPUs, confirming that physical quantum processors do not need a native square-grid lattice to achieve distance-scaling error suppression under topological quantum memory codes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Removes a long-assumed hardware constraint: surface-code QEC doesn't require redesigning chip connectivity to a square grid, which is significant for any hardware vendor not built on native square lattices.
insights.locator: the study confirms that physical quantum processors do not require a native square-grid lattice

insights.claim: The team used a depth-minimizing 'fold-unfold' SWAP embedding with bridge ancillas, combined with gap-aware robust dynamical decoupling implemented via Quantum Elements' Orbit Qiskit Function, to suppress the non-Markovian dephasing and coherent ZZ crosstalk that heavy-hex routing delays and idle gaps normally cause.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A reusable software-layer technique (Orbit Qiskit Function) for mitigating connectivity-driven noise, portable to other non-native-lattice QEC experiments on IBM hardware.
insights.locator: the research team co-designed a depth-minimizing

insights.claim: The surface code distance was scaled from d=3 (37 qubits) to anisotropic (dx, dz) = (3,5) and (5,3) configurations (65 qubits), executing up to 10 QEC cycles at circuit depth greater than 140 with 2,200 entangling gates.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Concrete scale benchmark (qubit count, cycle depth, gate count) investors can use to compare against competing QEC demonstrations from other hardware/software teams.
insights.locator: IBM Heavy-Hex Surface Code Demonstration & Benchmarking Metrics

insights.claim: The paper introduces an SPAM-aware Entanglement Fidelity (EF) metric, co-authored by Daniel Lidar (USC Center for Quantum Information Science & Technology Director and Quantum Elements CSO) and Arian Vezvaee, that isolates per-cycle logical error rates without assuming stationary noise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A new, more rigorous fidelity metric could become a standard for comparing QEC progress claims across hardware vendors, reducing apples-to-oranges benchmarking.
insights.locator: the paper introduces an SPAM-aware Entanglement Fidelity

insights.claim: The study explicitly warns against 'spurious subthreshold claims,' showing that unmitigated idle noise can falsely mimic genuine error-suppression scaling behavior if advanced dynamical decoupling is not integrated into hardware control sequences.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A methodological caution investors should apply when evaluating competitors' QEC scaling press releases: subthreshold claims without rigorous noise-mitigation controls may be artifacts, not real progress.

insights.claim: This heavy-hex surface code demonstration builds on a June 2026 USC/Quantum Elements paper in Physical Review Letters that used a Quantum Monte Carlo method to stochastically compress open-system density matrices and simulate 97-qubit surface code circuits without hitting the classical sign problem.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows a sustained, multi-year USC/Quantum Elements research roadmap moving from classical digital-twin simulation toward hardware-calibrated QEC design, useful for tracking this partnership's trajectory.
insights.locator: This experimental milestone builds on previous collaborative work
